_comment: One model policy for the whole fleet. Before this file there were four, and they
disagreed: CLAUDE.md order 17, hooks/model_gate.py's IMPL_MODEL, go.py's model_for()
and the Forge Phase 0 note. On 2026-09-03 that disagreement cost roughly $6,250 of
list-equivalent in four hours, because the one that won in practice -- go.py -- moved
a goal to Opus after two resumes, and a resume is what a bloated context causes.
So: a class decides the model, a brief may name a harder class, and nothing escalates
a tier by failing. Cost is calls x context x tier, and this file bounds all three.

and for the cost replay, not for billing: the fleet runs on a subscription, so the
number is a list-equivalent that makes one window comparable with another.

_audit_lens_timeout_comment: GATE.md item 3: the BBZ-99 round's correctness and scope-conformance lenses both
timed out at the bare fleet-wide 120s (reasoner.timeoutMs below) while the same
round's Codex lane, reviewing the identical diff, was budgeted 900s. audit-lens's
own timeoutMs is 480000ms (8 minutes): four times the old ceiling, so a large diff
that needed more than one turn's worth of thinking time actually finishes, and half
of Codex's 900s, because a lens is one isolated Sonnet turn on a packet Codex reviews
the same diff with a whole subprocess and its own tool calls -- it earns a real
budget, not the full 900s a heavier lane needs for more work per call.
_narrate_timeout_comment: R-23: narrate's timeoutMs is 180000ms, three times the fleet default, and that is a
generous number on purpose. Nothing waits on a narration -- every route answers from
the template the moment it is asked, and the sentence lands on a later poll -- so a
slow call costs a slower disclosure and nothing else. A tight one costs much more:
since a call that fails is cached as a refusal (never-by-retry, so a model that is
down cannot be re-bought by every board every few seconds), a call killed at 60s
while the box was busy freezes that fact record on its template for good. The live
proof on 2026-09-09 lost five of twenty specimens to exactly that. Slow is free here;
_governor_comment: P4.2: budgets Aaron sets, that the Governor queues against and never silently
exceeds. Generous on purpose -- these are a backstop against a run that would
otherwise spend unbounded, not a throttle on ordinary work. Exceeding one parks
the run (governor.parked evidence on a run.parked event), never kills it, and

_reasoner_comment: Added for Forge Intake (P4.3). astra: off is the shipped default -- the Intake
planner's plan seam always resolves to claude while this is off. Only
planning-only turns astra on, per the 2026-09-04 16:40 amendment (Aaron: limit
astra to what absolutely matters). No stream build, test, lens or review calls
astra regardless of this flag. timeoutMs bounds one Reasoner.call (P4.7/I4);
a call that outruns it is journaled as reasoner.timeout rather than left hanging.
_council_comment: forge-council-live: codex stays off by default (Aaron 2026-09-04 16:40: astra and
Codex are limited to what absolutely matters). allowedRepos and autoMerge are left
empty here on purpose -- this file is checked in and flightdeck stays project
agnostic (npm run check:agnostic scans every tracked file for a real repo name),
so a real entry for either list lives only in an operator's own environment
(FORGE_COUNCIL_REPOS, FORGE_COUNCIL_AUTOMERGE, both comma-separated) or a local,
untracked policy override, never here. Empty reads as fail-closed: review nothing,
merge nothing, until an operator configures it.
_conductor_comment: The Conductor agent behind the console rail (2026-09-08): one Sonnet session on the
implement class holding the console tools. enabled: true routes every typed message
to it, with the regex grammar as the fallback when the session cannot open or does
not answer inside reasoner.timeoutMs; false keeps every message on the grammar.
_rounds_comment: The Conductor's rounds (2026-09-08): every everyMinutes it walks the queue, the lanes
and the blocker board. apply: false only journals a rounds.sheet row and posts one rail
card when the findings change; apply: true clears rows whose PR merged, relaunches
workers with no process (at most maxRelaunches per item), restarts parked rows nothing
holds, archives finished lanes older than orphanHours with no queue row, and hands open
asks to the Conductor to answer or leave. silentMinutes is how long a running lane may
go without a process or an event before it counts as dead.
